content.value_statement: Distributed transactions fail when services cannot coordinate state safely. This skill provides saga templates for orchestration, choreography, compensation, and timeout handling.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to use saga orchestration for multi-service transactions.
Provides Python templates for saga state, steps, orchestration, and compensation.
Shows an order fulfillment saga with inventory, payment, shipping, and notification steps.
Includes choreography-based event handling examples for service coordination.
Adds timeout handling patterns for long-running saga steps.
limitations: Provides templates and guidance, not a packaged runtime or tested library.
Examples use abstract storage, event bus, scheduler, and service clients.
Does not include database schema, deployment instructions, or broker configuration.
Users must adapt retries, security, and observability to their systems.

use_cases.title: Design Order Fulfillment
use_cases.description: Create a workflow that reserves inventory, charges payment, ships items, and compensates failures.

use_cases.title: Standardize Service Workflows
use_cases.description: Define durable states, events, and timeout behavior for long-running work across services.

use_cases.title: Choose a Transaction Pattern
use_cases.description: Compare orchestration and choreography before selecting a distributed transaction approach.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Saga

prompt_templates.title: Adapt Order Fulfillment
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the skill to adapt the order fulfillment saga for [domain]. Replace services, commands, compensation steps, and failure events.

prompt_templates.title: Add Failure Handling
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the saga-orchestration skill to add retries, idempotency checks, and timeout behavior to this workflow: [workflow details].

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate Orchestration Strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the skill to compare orchestration and choreography for [system]. Recommend a design, describe tradeoffs, and list required safeguards.

output_examples.input: Order checkout saga for inventory, payment, shipping, and notification.
output_examples.output: A sequence of named saga steps with compensation paths for inventory release, payment refund, shipment cancellation, and customer cancellation notice.

output_examples.input: Payment service fails after inventory is reserved.
output: The order is marked failed with an auditable reason.

output_examples.input: Compare orchestration and choreography for a loan approval workflow.
output_examples.output: A recommendation explaining when a central orchestrator helps compliance, tracing, and timeout control, and when event choreography reduces coupling.

best_practices: Make every saga step idempotent so retries do not create duplicate business actions.
Test compensating transactions before production because they handle the most costly failures.
Use correlation identifiers, durable state, and logs for every saga transition.
anti_patterns: Treating a saga like a database transaction with instant rollback.
Skipping timeout behavior for steps that depend on remote services.
Publishing events without enough context to compensate or audit the workflow.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps design saga-based workflows for distributed transactions and long-running business processes.

faq.question: Does it install a saga framework?
faq.answer: No. It provides patterns and templates that you adapt to your own services and infrastructure.

faq.question: Does it support both orchestration and choreography?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains both approaches and includes examples for a central orchestrator and event-driven choreography.

faq.question: Which languages are shown?
faq.answer: The examples are written in Python-style pseudocode with abstract stores, event publishers, and schedulers.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is documented for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code compatible workflows.

faq.question: What should I customize before production?
faq.answer: Customize persistence, messaging, retries, idempotency, error handling, timeouts, authorization, and observability for your system.
